rubrics.justification: Mostly consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and appropriately notes possible partial collapse, but it overstates confidence in visible TE detail and comments on zona thinning/hatching that are not clearly discernible from this image.
Thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, sperm parameters, BMI, endometrium, and cycle context with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and structured, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context; minor tension exists between the image appearing less expanded and accepting the reported 3AA grade.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF practice, including SET preference and hydrosalpinx optimization, though some suggestions (e.g., sperm DNA fragmentation, embryo banking) are more conditional than guideline-driven.
Provides clear, practical next steps for current transfer management and contingency planning, including hydrosalpinx assessment, luteal support, follow-up timing, and future-cycle review points.
